newsitem.title: THAILAND: STA Group to raise capital, issue bonds.
newsitem.headline: STA Group to raise capital, issue bonds.

text.p: Thailand's troubled STA Group said on Wednesday it planned to raise registered capital to 12 billion (US$480 million) baht from 650 million baht through a new share issue at 10 baht each.
The company told the Thai stock exchange it also planned to issue 1.0 billion baht bonds attached with warrants through a private placement.
The SET on Wednesday suspended trading in shares of the company pending clarification about its restructuring plan.
The bond issue will have maturity of between three to five years and be offered at the coupon rate of between 4.00 to 6.00 percent per annum, said the STA Group which is a particle board maker.
Under the scheme, the company will also propose to swap existing secured loans of three billion baht into 100 new common shares.
Another 2.0 billion baht unsecured loans will be swapped into 40 million common shares, it said.
STA Group will also invite new investors into the company to provide management expertise and marketing networks to enable the turnaround of its troubled manufacturing operation.

The company's major shareholder, Rujirus Vilaipun, had also offered to to sell a substantial portion of his holdings to a Malaysian investor, Philip Ling, the controlling shareholder in Pan Pacific Asia Berhad, it said.
The company's board and financial advisor were currently negotiating with various involving parties on the planned restructuring, it added.
A Thai newspaper earlier on Wednesday quoted STA Group's president Kamol Poolsawat as saying that because of debts, the company's manufacturing operations had nearly stopped.
The newspaper estimated the firm's debts at around 11 billion baht. The company recently delayed repayment on its 1.1 billion baht in debentures issued to the public.
